readme.name: README.md
readme.html:
Tidewater

Notes, readings and photos from a season of watching one small harbor.

  • photos/ - the keepers, one per outing
  • data/ - raw gauge exports and the station map
  • src/ - the scripts that turn readings into charts

Start with field-notes.md.

archive.name: README.md
archive.html:
Gauge archive

One file a day per gauge, with a reading every ten minutes: <station>/<year>/<month>/<YYYY-MM-DD>.csv.

  • Heights are in metres above chart datum, with each gauge's offset already taken off
  • A day with no file is a day the gauge was down
  • summary.json in each month holds the highs, lows and ranges

Events

DateWhat
2026-02-11storm surge, +0.42 m at the peak
2025-11-03buoy 19 dragged 20 m east
2024-08-20east channel dredged, gauge resurveyed

maps.name: README.md
maps.html:
Maps

The harbor chart, drawn from the surveys, and cut into web map tiles.

  • harbor-chart.svg - the whole chart, one file
  • charts/ - a small chart around each station
  • tiles/<z>/<x>/<y>.png - zoom 0 to 8, rendered by harbor/scripts/render-tiles.sh

recordings.name: README.md
recordings.html:
Recordings

Hydrophones on six moorings, recording a few minutes every few hours: <site>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<hh-mm>.flac. A .json beside a recording marks something worth hearing.

scans.name: README.md
scans.html:
Scans

The harbor master's tide logbooks, 1961 to 1988, one folder per book. raw/ holds the full-size TIFFs and is left out of the search by .okfsignore.

harbor.name: README.md
harbor.html:
harbor

The code behind tidewater: the gauge daemon, the archive, the chart tiles and the site.

PathWhat
apps/the site, the dashboard, the API, the daemon
packages/shared TypeScript: tides, charts, ui
crates/Rust: harmonics, the gauge protocol, tiles
docs/how it fits together
bun install
bun run dev        # the site and the dashboard
cargo run -p gauge-daemon

Changelog

2.14.0

  • levelAt draws between the two readings around a time, instead of taking the nearest
  • turns smooths over three readings first, so a gust no longer makes a false high water
  • New: rangeOf(day) for the high and low of one day in one call

2.13.2

  • Fix: a station with no readings for a day no longer throws in turns

2.13.0

  • Readings carry their gauge's offset, so a height is right even when the gauge moves
  • Heights round to the centimetre in formatHeight, as the tide tables do

Adding a gauge

A gauge is a staff gauge with a logger strapped to it, on a piling or a buoy. Adding one takes three steps.

1. Survey it in

Read the staff against a known benchmark at two low waters and two high waters. The difference is the gauge's offset, in centimetres. Write it down.

2. Name it

Add it to gauges.toml:

[[gauge]]
station = "mill-creek"
offset_cm = -4
depth_m = 2.1

3. Watch it

gauge-daemon picks it up on its next start and writes a file a day to archive/mill-creek/. The dashboard shows it once it has a full day.

Tidal harmonics: the height of the tide as a sum of cosines, one per constituent.use std::f64::consts::PI;/// One constituent of the tide at a station: how high it swings and where it is in its cycle.#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]pub struct Constituent { pub name: &'static str, /// Degrees per hour. pub speed: f64, /// Metres. pub amplitude: f64, /// Degrees, against the station's epoch. pub phase: f64,}/// The constituents that carry most of the tide in a small harbor.pub const MAJOR: [(&str, f64); 6] = [ ("M2", 28.984_104_2), ("S2", 30.0), ("N2", 28.439_729_5), ("K1", 15.041_068_6), ("O1", 13.943_035_6), ("M4", 57.968_208_4),];pub struct Station { pub name: String, /// Mean sea level above chart datum, in metres. pub mean: f64, pub constituents: Vec<Constituent>,}impl Station { /// The predicted height `hours` after the station's epoch. pub fn height(&self, hours: f64) -> f64 { self.mean + self .constituents .iter() .map(|c| c.amplitude * ((c.speed * hours - c.phase) * PI / 180.0).cos()) .sum::<f64>() } /// High and low waters over `span` hours, found by stepping a minute at a time. pub fn turns(&self, from: f64, span: f64) -> Vec<(f64, f64, bool)> { let step = 1.0 / 60.0; let mut out = Vec::new(); let (mut before, mut here) = (self.height(from - step), self.height(from)); let mut t = from; while t < from + span { let after = self.height(t + step); if (here > before) != (after > here) { out.push((t, here, here > before)); } (before, here, t) = (here, after, t + step); } out }}#[cfg(test)]mod tests { use super::*; #[test] fn a_pure_m2_tide_turns_four_times_a_day() { let station = Station { name: "test".into(), mean: 1.9, constituents: vec![Constituent { name: "M2", speed: MAJOR[0].1, amplitude: 1.4, phase: 0.0 }], }; assert_eq!(station.turns(0.0, 24.0).len(), 4); }}","lines":75,"highlighted":true}

Every height is in metres above chart datum.export interface Reading { /** Minutes since midnight, local time at the station. */ minute: number; /** As the staff gauge reads it, in centimetres. */ rawCm: number; offsetCm: number;}export const corrected = (reading: Reading): number => (reading.rawCm - reading.offsetCm) / 100;/** The height at `at`, drawn from the two readings around it. */export function levelAt(readings: Reading[], at: number): number { const minute = new Date(at).getHours() * 60 + new Date(at).getMinutes(); const after = readings.findIndex((reading) => reading.minute >= minute); if (after <= 0) return corrected(readings[Math.max(after, 0)] ?? readings[readings.length - 1]); const a = readings[after - 1]; const b = readings[after]; const share = (minute - a.minute) / (b.minute - a.minute); return corrected(a) + (corrected(b) - corrected(a)) * share;}/** High and low water of one day: the turning points, not just the largest and smallest values. */export function turns(readings: Reading[]): { at: number; height: number; high: boolean }[] { const heights = smooth(readings.map(corrected), 3); const out = []; for (let i = 1; i < heights.length - 1; i++) { const rising = heights[i] > heights[i - 1]; const falling = heights[i + 1] < heights[i]; if (rising === falling) out.push({ at: readings[i].minute, height: heights[i], high: rising }); } return out;}function smooth(values: number[], width: number): number[] { return values.map((_, i) => { const from = Math.max(0, i - width); const window = values.slice(from, i + width + 1); return window.reduce((sum, v) => sum + v, 0) / window.length; });}","lines":42,"highlighted":true}

{"kind":"code","html":""""Backfills the archive from the gauges' own memory after a network outage."""import argparseimport csvfrom datetime import date, timedeltafrom pathlib import Pathfrom harbor.gauges import connectdef backfill(station: str, since: date, archive: Path) -> int: gauge = connect(station) written = 0 day = since while day < date.today(): target = archive / station / f"{day:%Y}" / f"{day:%m}" / f"{day:%Y-%m-%d}.csv" if not target.exists(): target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) with target.open("w", newline="") as f: out = csv.writer(f) out.writerow(["time", "raw_cm", "height_m", "battery"]) for reading in gauge.memory(day): out.writerow([reading.time, reading.raw_cm, reading.height_m, reading.battery]) written += 1 day += timedelta(days=1) return writtenif __name__ == "__main__": parser = argparse.ArgumentParser() parser.add_argument("station") parser.add_argument("--since", type=date.fromisoformat, required=True) parser.add_argument("--archive", type=Path, default=Path("archive")) args = parser.parse_args() print(f"wrote {backfill(args.station, args.since, args.archive)} days")","lines":35,"highlighted":true}

# Changelog

## 2.14.0

- `levelAt` draws between the two readings around a time, instead of taking the nearest
- `turns` smooths over three readings first, so a gust no longer makes a false high water
- New: `rangeOf(day)` for the high and low of one day in one call

## 2.13.2

- Fix: a station with no readings for a day no longer throws in `turns`

## 2.13.0

- Readings carry their gauge's offset, so a height is right even when the gauge moves
- Heights round to the centimetre in `formatHeight`, as the tide tables do

# Adding a gauge

A gauge is a staff gauge with a logger strapped to it, on a piling or a buoy. Adding one takes
three steps.

## 1. Survey it in

Read the staff against a known benchmark at two low waters and two high waters. The difference is
the gauge's **offset**, in centimetres. Write it down.

## 2. Name it

Add it to `gauges.toml`:

```toml
[[gauge]]
station = "mill-creek"
offset_cm = -4
depth_m = 2.1
```

## 3. Watch it

`gauge-daemon` picks it up on its next start and writes a file a day to
`archive/mill-creek/`. The dashboard shows it once it has a full day.

"""Backfills the archive from the gauges' own memory after a network outage."""

import argparse
import csv
from datetime import date, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

from harbor.gauges import connect


def backfill(station: str, since: date, archive: Path) -> int:
    gauge = connect(station)
    written = 0
    day = since
    while day < date.today():
        target = archive / station / f"{day:%Y}" / f"{day:%m}" / f"{day:%Y-%m-%d}.csv"
        if not target.exists():
            target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            with target.open("w", newline="") as f:
                out = csv.writer(f)
                out.writerow(["time", "raw_cm", "height_m", "battery"])
                for reading in gauge.memory(day):
                    out.writerow([reading.time, reading.raw_cm, reading.height_m, reading.battery])
            written += 1
        day += timedelta(days=1)
    return written


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("station")
    parser.add_argument("--since", type=date.fromisoformat, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--archive", type=Path, default=Path("archive"))
    args = parser.parse_args()
    print(f"wrote {backfill(args.station, args.since, args.archive)} days")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Renders the chart tiles again from the latest survey, then checks that every zoom level is whole.
set -euo pipefail

survey=${1:-surveys/latest.geojson}
out=maps/tiles

echo "rendering $survey into $out"
cargo run --release -p tile-render -- --survey "$survey" --out "$out" --max-zoom 8

for z in $(seq 0 8); do
  want=$(( (1 << z) * (1 << z) ))
  have=$(find "$out/$z" -name '*.png' | wc -l)
  if [ "$have" -ne "$want" ]; then
    echo "zoom $z has $have tiles, wants $want" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done
echo "all tiles in place"
